name: Belmond Hotel Monasterio
positioning: Monasterio, a former 16th-century baroque monastery in Cusco built on Inca foundations, with courtyards, Cusco School art and two restaurants
best_for: Travelers drawn to Cusco's history who want to stay in a former monastery
Guests who enjoy art and a courtyard setting

facts.text: The hotel is a former 16th-century baroque monastery.
In 1595 the site became the San Antonio Abad Monastery.
The hotel opened as a luxury hotel in 1965.
Oqre serves Peruvian cuisine with a twist.
El Tupay serves international fine dining.
The hotel has an ornate baroque chapel.
The hotel has a spa treatment suite.
The hotel is a 20 minute drive from Alejandro Velasco Astete Airport (CUZ).
The hotel is a 3.5 hour train ride from Machu Picchu.
Condé Nast Traveler lists Readers' Choice Awards for the hotel in 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2023 and 2026.

highlights.text: The hotel rests on the original foundations of Inca Emperor Amaru Qhata's palace.
The courtyards are gathered around a 300-year-old Andean cedar.
Guests can dine under stone arches to the sound of live opera in El Tupay.
The hotel has a collection of prized Cusco School art.

considerations.text: The hotel is a 20 minute drive from the airport and a 3.5 hour train ride from Machu Picchu, so Machu Picchu is a separate trip.
Spa facilities are a single spa treatment suite rather than a full spa.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Monasterio, A Belmond Hotel, Cusco
